shape.text: A secret access token is a string of three dot-delimited parts (header, payload, signature) whose header is the literal sk.
The payload is a base64url-encoded JSON object that holds a reference to the metadata recording the token's rights, not the metadata itself.
The signature part is signed by Mapbox so that tampering can be detected.

issuance.text: The value of a secret token can be copied only once, when the token is created, and the Tokens API leaves the token value out of its listing for secret tokens.
Secret scopes cannot be added to a public token; a token that needs secret scopes is created as a new secret token.
The provider says requests that need a token with secret scopes must be made on a server, and that such tokens must not be exposed to the client.

lifecycle.text: A token can be deleted and replaced at any time, and the provider advises rotating tokens when misuse is suspected.

collisions.text: A public access token has the same three-part shape with the header pk, and the provider documents public tokens as designed for client-side applications and safe to expose in browsers and apps.
A token's id, shown in the account dashboard and in token listings, identifies a token and is not the access token itself.

openQuestions.text: What length do the payload and signature parts have, and what encoding does the signature use?

unresolved.reason: The documentation gives no length for the payload or signature part and no encoding for the signature, and no token was issued to observe them.

openQuestions.text: Has the secret token format changed over time, so that older tokens have a different shape?

unresolved.reason: The documentation pages and the Accounts service changelog read list no change to the sk header or token shape, which is the absence of a statement rather than a statement that the format never changed.
